# Acceptance matrix

This file is the normative oracle for the acceptance corpus. Each row names a
fixture construct and its expected behavior at the boundaries exercised by the
MVP. A dash means that the construct must have no independently observable
behavior in that column; it does not mean that the behavior is unspecified.

The tables use canonical, directory-style URLs. A route ending in `/` is written
as an `index.html` file beneath that directory. API routes use the extracted
qualified name beneath `/packages/<slug>/api/`; authored routes retain the path
beneath the collection mount; and concept routes use `/concepts/<id>/`. These
routes are independent of semantic IDs.

The following invariants apply to every row:

- `diplodocus check` parses, extracts, and validates the construct but never starts
  a language runtime or kernel, reads or writes the execution cache, writes
  execution assets, or creates the output directory.
- `None` in the Diagnostic column means that the construct itself produces no
  diagnostic. A row naming a diagnostic gives the sole intentional diagnostic
  for that focused invalid construct; unrelated diagnostics fail its test.
- Every source location contains a repository ID and normalized,
  forward-slash-separated repository-relative path, plus a span where the
  source format supplies one. Portable IR, diagnostics, provenance, rendered
  output, and search data contain no absolute checkout or temporary paths.
- Repository provenance contains the configured canonical URL, revision, dirty
  state when available, and a fingerprint of declared inputs. Extracted API
  provenance also contains extractor identity, version, capabilities, static
  mode, and relevant parser versions. Authored provenance contains the content
  format and Panache version. Executed output provenance additionally contains
  engine and kernel identities and versions, normalized options, declared
  environment fingerprints, the producing cell, and fresh-or-cache status.
- A public item is linkable, appears in its ecosystem-aware package navigation,
  and contributes a search entry containing its package and ecosystem. An
  internal item is linkable and searchable but its unit is absent from the
  project package switcher. A hidden item is linkable by semantic ID but absent
  from navigation and search.
- Authored source links, ordinary relative links, and semantic references are
  validated. Search indexes authored titles and prose, API qualified names,
  signatures, and documentation—not code-cell output or unsupported raw
  syntax.

## MVP completion coverage

| MVP criterion | Proving matrix rows |
| --- | --- |
| One explicit polyglot workspace configuration | Workspace and configuration rows for repositories, packages, targets, content, execution, relationships, concepts, and variants |
| Static Python and R API extraction | All Python API and R API rows, including stub precedence, dispatch families, and the two explicit unsupported cases |
| In-process GFM and Quarto parsing with visible unsupported syntax | All Authored content rows, especially the GFM component and QMD directive rows |
| Explicit Python and R Jupyter execution with structured results | Stateful Python and R rows and their stream, error, Markdown, and figure rows |
| One safe renderer, shared navigation, links, concepts, and search | Every URL, Navigation, Link, Concept, and Search column; output-safety rows define the trust boundaries |
| Command contract | The common check invariant and the execution modes in the workspace and execution rows |
| Deterministic, portable builds | Common provenance invariants plus content-addressed assets, declared environment fingerprints, and fresh-or-cache parity |
| No installs, implicit network access, or implicit authored execution | Static API rows, default-never and metadata-authority rows, and explicit execution-collection rows |
| Full acceptance test stack | This matrix is consumed by focused, golden, integration, link, search, and end-to-end tests as their behavior is implemented |
| Self-documentation and new-user workflow | Exercised by Diplodocus's own later dogfood corpus; no acceptance fixture construct currently claims to prove these project-level deliverables |
